missing_details: Specification that the gauge group G must be a compact simple Lie group
The requirement that the theory be defined on four-dimensional Euclidean space ℝ⁴
That the quantum Yang–Mills theory must be non-trivial and non-abelian
That existence entails constructing a rigorously defined QFT satisfying axiomatic frameworks (e.g., Wightman or Osterwalder–Schrader axioms)
The precise meaning of the mass gap Δ>0 as the lowest non-zero eigenvalue of the energy (mass) operator corresponding to the lightest particle
refined_question: Let G be any compact simple Lie group. Construct a non-trivial quantum Yang–Mills theory on four-dimensional Euclidean space ℝ⁴ that satisfies the standard axioms of quantum field theory (for example, the Wightman axioms or Osterwalder–Schrader axioms). Prove that the spectrum of the corresponding Hamiltonian H has a strictly positive mass gap Δ, meaning that apart from the vacuum state of zero energy, the infimum of the spectrum of H is bounded below by Δ>0.
justification: The name “Yang–Mills existence and mass gap” indicates the dual goals of proving the existence of a Yang–Mills theory and establishing a mass gap, but it does not specify critical elements such as the gauge group (compact simple Lie group G), the four-dimensional Euclidean domain, the requirement of non-abelian, non-trivial QFT, the necessity of rigorous axiomatic construction, or the definition of the mass gap as the lowest positive energy eigenvalue. These details are essential for a precise, standalone formulation.
